steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Cenozoic Era (66 Ma to present) is the 'Age of Mammals' — mammals diversified after the dinosaurs went extinct

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Quaternary Period (2.6 Ma to present) includes the Pleistocene (repeated glaciations) and the Holocene (last 11,700 years, current interglacial)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: During the Pleistocene, there were multiple glacial (cold) and interglacial (warm) cycles driven by Milankovitch orbital variations

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The last glacial maximum was ~20,000 years ago; ice sheets covered much of Britain down to the Midlands

steps.title: Try it yourself

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Cenozoic = Age of Mammals (after dinosaurs died out at K-Pg boundary) Pleistocene = repeated glaciations; Holocene = current warm period Milankovitch cycles drive glacial-interglacial cycles British landscape: U-valleys, drumlins, erratics, till all indicate glaciation
